skill.name: command-optimization
skill.description: Designs and improves command-line interfaces, including command names, argument structures, automation workflows, help text, and error handling.
skill.summary: Designs and improves CLI commands, arguments, help text, and slash command templates.
skill.author: Joseph OBrien

security_audit.summary: Most static findings in SKILL.md are false positives from Markdown fences, inline option names, and documented examples. The reference template contains real slash-command dynamic context using shell commands that execute when copied into a command. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or malicious command content was found.

remediation.issue: Dynamic shell context can execute local commands when a slash command loads.
remediation.suggestion: Add safety guidance to use only deterministic read-only commands, avoid user input, and restrict allowed tools narrowly.

remediation.issue: Template placeholders allow arbitrary shell commands in generated slash commands.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to remove placeholders and review every shell command before publishing a generated command.

remediation.issue: Shell command examples lack an explicit safety warning.
remediation.suggestion: Mark examples as documentation and add a short warning before dynamic context examples.

finding_verdicts.reason: The reference documents slash-command dynamic context with shell commands that execute when a command loads. The examples are benign, but the pattern enables load-time external command execution in generated commands.

semantic_findings.title: Load-Time Shell Execution in Slash Command Template
semantic_findings.description: The slash command template tells users to use dynamic context shell commands that execute when a command loads. This can run local commands if a generated command keeps unsafe dynamic context or accepts unreviewed shell placeholders.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly states that dynamic context shell commands execute when the command loads. The examples are read-only, so the risk is contextual rather than evidence of malicious intent.

content.value_statement: CLI commands often grow inconsistent, unclear, or hard to maintain. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design usable commands, arguments, error handling, and documentation.
actual_capabilities: Designs task-oriented CLI command names, options, and usage patterns.
Reviews command examples for clearer arguments and safer defaults.
Drafts help text, error messages, and usage documentation.
Creates slash command templates with frontmatter, arguments, workflows, and output formats.
Explains validation, dry-run, confirmation, and verbose-mode patterns.
limitations: It provides guidance and templates, not a tested CLI framework.
It does not include executable scripts or argument-parsing libraries.
Dynamic shell context in slash command templates requires careful review before use.
Generated commands still need project-specific implementation and tests.

use_cases.title: Create Developer Commands
use_cases.description: Design a new project command with clear usage, options, examples, and validation rules.

use_cases.title: Improve Existing CLI Workflows
use_cases.description: Review confusing commands and refine names, flags, feedback, and error messages.

use_cases.title: Standardize Slash Command Templates
use_cases.description: Draft reusable slash command structure with frontmatter, arguments, workflow steps, and output format.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Command
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple CLI command for [task]. Include the command name, purpose, required arguments, optional flags, and one usage example.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Command Interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this command: [command]. Improve the name, arguments, options, help text, validation, and error messages.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Safe Slash Command Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a slash command template for [workflow]. Include frontmatter, arguments, workflow steps, output format, and safety notes for any dynamic context.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Command Suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a command suite for [project workflow]. Define consistent command names, shared options, validation rules, dry-run behavior, and documentation structure.

output_examples.input: Create a command for generating React components.
output: A task-focused command name with a clear component target.
Recommended options for path, component type, tests, and styles.
Validation guidance for missing names and invalid output paths.

output_examples.input: Improve a vague dependency check command.
output: A clearer command name that states the analysis goal.
Output format options for summary and detailed results.
Actionable error messages and next-step recommendations.

output_examples.input: Create a slash command template for project cleanup.
output: Frontmatter fields for description, argument hint, and tool limits.
A structured workflow with current state, task steps, and final output.
A safety reminder for any dynamic shell context.

best_practices: Start with a clear action verb, target object, and one primary task.
Add dry-run, confirmation, and validation for commands that change files or data.
Keep examples, help text, and error messages aligned with real project conventions.
anti_patterns: Using vague command names such as check, run, or make without context.
Adding force or rollback options without safeguards or clear warnings.
Copying dynamic shell context into slash commands without reviewing what executes.

faq.question: Does this skill write production CLI code?
faq.answer: It drafts command designs, examples, and guidance. You still need to implement and test the final code.

faq.question: Can it help with argument parsing?
faq.answer: Yes. It can design arguments, options, defaults, validation rules, and help text.

faq.question: Does it support slash commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a slash command template with frontmatter, arguments, workflow sections, and output format guidance.

faq.question: Is dynamic shell context safe?
faq.answer: It can be useful, but every shell command must be reviewed and limited to safe read-only behavior.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Developers, tool maintainers, and AI workflow authors can use it to improve command design.

faq.question: What tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
